intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A feast for all the senses and a true taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the legendary Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small islet, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful coastal settings. Accessible by local bus or rental car.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local Cretan family or chef, learning to prepare traditional dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and homemade phyllo pastries. Includes a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients and ends with a communal meal paired with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Sunset Taverna Dinner in Oia
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from the cliffside village of Oia, then dine at a traditional taverna serving fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea dip), tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and locally caught fish. Pair your meal with a glass of crisp Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini's volcanic vineyards for an authentic and unforgettable evening.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs and collect luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea right outside the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the nearest waterfront promenade, browse local souvenir shops, and soak in the sunset over the sea. Explore the immediate neighbourhood around the resort.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or a cheese-and-spinach spanakopita from a nearby bakery or street kiosk close to the resort (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Find a simple taverna near the beachfront — order grilled octopus, Greek salad, and house wine. Look for the daily special (mageirefta) for best value (€10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed to recover from travel. Exchange some cash at the airport or use a fee-free card for best rates. Keep dinner casual and close to the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim at the resort beach before crowds arrive. Explore the shoreline on foot — look for quieter coves or rocky outcrops nearby. Bring snorkel gear if available (many resorts rent cheaply).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local market or farmers' market. Pick up fresh fruit, olives, local cheese, and bread for a DIY picnic lunch on the beach. Browse local produce and chat with vendors for an authentic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost sunset viewing spot — a hilltop, a harbour wall, or a clifftop near the resort. Afterwards, try a local ouzeri (ouzo bar) for a small plate of mezedes and a glass of ouzo or tsipouro.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or a sesame-coated koulouri bread ring and Greek coffee from a street vendor (€2–3)
meals.lunch: DIY picnic from the local market — feta, olives, tomatoes, bread, and fresh fruit (€5–7 total)
meals.dinner: Ouzeri mezedes platter: tzatziki, taramosalata, grilled bread, and a carafe of local wine shared between two (€8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Markets usually run in the morning and close by early afternoon. Bring a reusable bag and small cash. Mezedes portions are generous — order gradually to avoid overspending.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared taxi to a nearby archaeological site or ancient ruins (most Greek destinations have one within 30–60 minutes). Explore early before the heat peaks. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort area and spend the hottest hours (13:00–16:00) at the beach. Try snorkelling in the clear Aegean water — sea is warm and visibility is excellent in June.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the old town or village quarter nearest to the resort. Browse whitewashed alleyways, small chapels, and craft shops. Settle into a taverna for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek yoghurt with local honey and walnuts at a café near the resort (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and chips from a local grill house near the ruins or back at the resort (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner: moussaka or pastitsio, village salad, and a half-litre of house red or white wine (€11–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check bus schedules the night before — rural Greek buses can be infrequent. Archaeological sites often have free entry on the first Sunday of the month. Carry a printed or offline map.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter from a local rental shop (€8–15/day) and explore the coastal road. Discover hidden beaches and fishing villages that are harder to reach on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a secluded or less-touristed beach spotted during the morning ride. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing. Bring packed snacks and water.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes/scooters and head to a harbour-side fish taverna. Watch fishing boats come in and enjoy the freshest catch of the day at local prices.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) and a freddo espresso at a local kafeneio (traditional café) (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from the morning market or a simple sandwich from a bakery to eat at the beach (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Harbour fish taverna: grilled fresh fish (priced by weight — choose smaller fish like sardines or mackerel for budget value), chips, and salad (€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental requires a valid licence in Greece. Bicycles are a cheaper alternative. Always negotiate rental rates — daily rates are often lower than posted prices. Wear sunscreen on exposed skin during the coastal ride.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike on a local coastal or nature trail. Many Greek coastal areas have well-marked paths with stunning sea views. Start early (07:00–08:00) to beat the heat. Carry at least 1.5 litres of water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool down with a long swim at a beach at the end of the trail or back at the resort. Relax under a beach umbrella (rent one for €3–5 if not included with resort).
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble your own meal using ingredients from the local market — a great budget hack. Alternatively, find a psistaria (grill house) for inexpensive grilled meats.

meals.breakfast: Homemade-style: fresh bread, local honey, feta, and tomatoes bought from the market the day before (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks: nuts, dried fruit, and a local energy bar, plus a cold freddo cappuccino at a café at the trail end (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Psistaria grilled pork souvlaki skewers or lamb chops with pita and salad — hearty and affordable (€9–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Download an offline trail map (AllTrails or Maps.me) before heading out. Let someone at the resort know your hiking route. Avoid hiking between 12:00–15:00 in 29°C heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local ferry or boat trip to a nearby island or sea cave (many Greek coastal resorts offer short boat excursions for €10–20). Book at the harbour the evening before for best prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip island or sea cave on foot — most are small enough to walk around in a few hours. Swim in crystal-clear water and explore rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry before sunset. Enjoy a quiet dinner back near the resort, reflecting on the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Quick stop at a bakery before the ferry — loukoumades (honey doughnuts) or a fresh croissant with Greek coffee (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch on the boat or buy from a small kiosk on the day-trip island — simple sandwiches and fruit (€5–7)
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna back at base: stuffed tomatoes and peppers (gemista), village bread, and local beer (€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book boat trips directly at the harbour to avoid agency markups. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. Pack sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the boat ride. Confirm return times before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the resort beach — you've earned it. Read a book, swim at your own pace, and enjoy a slow start. This is a mid-trip reset day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cooking class or food tour if available in the area (some budget options run €15–25 per person and include tastings). Alternatively, visit a local olive oil producer or winery for a free or low-cost tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different neighbourhood or village within easy reach of the resort. Find a lively local square (plateia) where Greeks gather in the evenings and join the volta (evening stroll).

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast if included, or a sit-down café breakfast: eggs, feta, olives, tomatoes, and Greek coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach bar: a Greek salad and a cold beer or fresh juice (€7–9)
meals.dinner: Join locals at a busy plateia taverna — order the daily special board for best value. Try revithia (chickpea soup) or fasolada (bean soup) for an ultra-budget authentic option (€8–11 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a deliberate slow day. Overplanning every day on a budget trip leads to fatigue and impulse spending. The volta is free and one of the most authentic Greek experiences — simply walk, observe, and enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local bus to a larger nearby town or city. Explore the central market (agora), browse local shops, and visit a free public museum or historic church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander the town's old quarter. Visit a Byzantine church, a Venetian fortress, or a historic landmark. Many are free to enter or have minimal entry fees (€2–4).
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in the town before catching the last bus back. Eating in slightly larger towns often gives more variety at similar budget prices.

meals.breakfast: On the bus or at the resort before departure — pack a yoghurt and fruit
meals.lunch: Central market lunch: fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and olives bought from stalls (€5–7)
meals.dinner: In the day-trip town: a mezedes spread at a traditional restaurant — saganaki (fried cheese), dolmades, and grilled vegetables with wine (€11–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check the last bus return time before you leave — missing it means an expensive taxi. Keep a small offline map of the town. Carry a lightweight day bag with water, sunscreen, and a phone charger.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk at sunrise — one of the most magical and free experiences in Greece. Collect sea glass or shells, photograph the golden light, and have the beach almost entirely to yourself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a water sport available at the resort beach: paddleboarding, kayaking, or windsurfing. Introductory sessions are often available for €10–20. Alternatively, rent a kayak and explore the coastline independently.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop or rooftop bar — budget one drink each and enjoy the atmosphere without overspending. Then dinner at a favourite taverna from earlier in the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café near the beach: fresh orange juice, a warm cheese pie, and Greek mountain tea (€4–5)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar: grilled corn, a cold frappe, and a simple sandwich (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Return to a favourite budget taverna discovered earlier — familiarity helps you order smarter and avoid tourist-menu markups (€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Water sport prices are often negotiable, especially later in the afternoon when instructors have fewer bookings. Sunrise is around 05:45–06:00 in mid-June in Greece — set an alarm if you want to catch it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local monastery or hilltop chapel — most are free to enter and offer breathtaking panoramic views. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees). These are often overlooked by tourists and beautifully peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a beach further from the resort — take a local bus or walk if within 3–4 km. Less-visited beaches often have cleaner water and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free local cultural event if one is happening (check local noticeboards or ask at the resort — summer festivals, outdoor cinema, and live music are common in June). Otherwise, enjoy a quiet waterfront dinner.

meals.breakfast: Simple and cheap: a koulouri from a street vendor and a takeaway Greek coffee (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the resort area bakery: spanakopita, a hard-boiled egg, fruit, and water (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Seaside restaurant: grilled sea bream or red mullet with lemon and olive oil, horta (wild greens), and local wine (€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monastery visiting hours are typically 08:00–13:00 and 17:00–20:00. Always check before making the trip. Local cultural events in summer are often listed on municipal websites or posted in the village square.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning — this is your dedicated relaxation day on the water. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the warm June sea. Bring your own snacks and drinks to avoid beach bar markups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local craft or artisan shop — look for handmade ceramics, leather sandals (a Greek staple), or locally produced honey and olive oil. These make great budget-friendly souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Try cooking a simple Greek meal yourself if your accommodation has any kitchen access, or arrange a shared meal with fellow travellers. Otherwise, find a no-frills local grill for a final mid-trip splurge.

meals.breakfast: Greek yoghurt with local thyme honey and fresh figs from the market (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Beach DIY: pre-packed olives, feta, tomatoes, and pita bread from a supermarket (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Local grill house: mixed meat platter with pita, tzatziki, and salad — great value for a slightly more indulgent evening (€13–17 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 is intentionally unstructured — some of the best travel memories come from unplanned moments. Allow yourself to wander, chat with locals, and follow curiosity rather than a strict schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: take a longer excursion to a landmark you haven't visited yet — a famous beach, a gorge walk, or a historic site. Use local transport to keep costs low.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last long swim in the Aegean. Take photos, float on your back, and savour the warm sea before the trip ends. Visit your favourite beach spot one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself slightly more than usual but still keep it authentic. Choose a taverna you loved during the trip and order dishes you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Full sit-down café breakfast: omelette with local herbs and feta, toast, juice, and coffee (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the excursion destination — souvlaki wrap or a simple salad (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell taverna dinner: lamb kleftiko or slow-cooked goat, a shared bottle of local wine, baklava for dessert (€15–20 per person — a modest splurge for the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Start packing non-essentials tonight to make Day 13 departure smoother. Check your flight time and arrange any transport to the airport in advance. Keep €20–30 in cash for airport expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — a quiet goodbye to the Aegean. Pack remaining items, check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, and store luggage with reception if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: spend remaining hours at the beach or in a nearby café. Pick up any last-minute local food souvenirs — vacuum-packed olives, local honey, or herbal tea from a deli or supermarket.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport. Reflect on 13 days of beaches, local food, and authentic Greek experiences. Board your return flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast: a warm cheese or spinach pie and a freddo espresso at a beachfront café (€4–5)
meals.lunch: Light and portable: a gyros wrap or a bakery sandwich to eat before heading to the airport (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Airport meal if needed — or save money with snacks packed earlier. Airport food is always more expensive, so budget €10–15 if you need a full meal there

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Keep all receipts if claiming travel expenses. Total estimated daily food budget across the trip: €20–35 per person per day, keeping the full 13-day food budget under €400 per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea to unwind after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest village on foot. Browse small shops and soak in the atmosphere as the sun sets over the water.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyro or souvlaki wrap from a local street food stall near the resort area upon arrival (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a waterfront taverna close to the resort. Try grilled octopus, Greek salad, and a carafe of local house wine (~€20-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Hydrate well after flying. Exchange some euros at the airport if needed. The sea temperature is ideal for swimming throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort, then head to the nearest main beach. Swim, snorkel, and relax in the warm morning sun before the midday heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a sun lounger and umbrella on the beach (~€8-10). Take a short walk to explore the coastal path and find a quieter cove for a more private swim.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local harbour area at sunset. Watch fishing boats return and enjoy the golden light over the water.

meals.breakfast: Buffet or à la carte breakfast at the resort (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a casual beach taverna — try fried calamari and tzatziki with pita (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a family-run restaurant in the village. Order moussaka or pastitsio with a Greek salad (~€18-24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen throughout the day. Average high is 29°C so mornings and late afternoons are the most comfortable for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Join a half-day boat trip or local snorkeling excursion departing from the nearby harbour. Explore sea caves and crystal-clear coves inaccessible by land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat trip and relax at the resort pool or beach. Read, nap, or enjoy a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the town centre for a traditional Greek evening stroll (volta). Browse the main pedestrian street and stop for a cold freddo espresso or frappe.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort or a local bakery — try a tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee (~€5-7)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or light bites on the boat, or grab a quick mezze platter at a harbour-side café upon return (~€12-16)
meals.dinner: Try a local taverna specialising in fresh catch of the day. Ask the waiter what fish came in that morning (~€22-30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat excursion the day before to secure a spot. Bring water, a hat, and reef-safe sunscreen for the boat trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or hire a local taxi for a morning drive to a scenic viewpoint or hilltop village nearby. Explore narrow cobblestone streets, whitewashed houses, and a small local church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a secluded or less-crowded beach on the way back, recommended by locals. Swim and unwind before returning to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor cultural event if available (check local notice boards), or simply enjoy a sunset cocktail at a cliffside bar.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort to fuel the day (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a village kafeneion (traditional coffee house/taverna). Try slow-cooked lamb or stuffed vegetables (gemista) (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Mezze-style dinner — order a spread of small dishes: hummus, dolmades, spanakopita, grilled halloumi, and olives (~€18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental typically costs €20-30/day. Carry a paper map or offline maps as rural areas may have poor mobile signal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local open-air market (laiki agora) if it falls on a market day. Browse fresh produce, local honey, olives, herbs, and handmade goods. Great for picking up affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a long afternoon swim. Try paddleboarding or kayaking rented from a beach vendor (~€10-15/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or food tour if available locally, or visit a traditional ouzo or wine bar and sample local spirits with small bites.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries and fruit from the market for a picnic-style breakfast (~€4-6)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market finds — local cheese, olives, bread, tomatoes, and fruit (~€8-12 total)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-reviewed mid-range restaurant. Try lamb chops (paidakia), roasted potatoes, and a local Assyrtiko white wine (~€24-32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Markets typically run early morning to early afternoon. Bring a reusable bag for purchases. Tipping 10% at restaurants is appreciated but not mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby archaeological site or ancient ruins. Explore at a relaxed pace, reading about the history of the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a traditional village on the return journey. Visit a small Byzantine church or monastery if accessible, and admire local architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Enjoy a sunset swim in the sea, then unwind on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna near the archaeological site — try a simple Greek salad, bread, and grilled chicken (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby souvlaki spot. Try chicken souvlaki with pita and tzatziki (~€12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for walking on ancient stone surfaces. Bring water and a hat. Many sites open early and close in the afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and beach morning. Sleep in, have a slow breakfast, and spend the morning swimming and sunbathing — a true mid-trip recharge day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby beach that requires a short hike or boat ride to reach. The effort rewards you with fewer crowds and clearer water.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner reservation at a highly rated local seafood restaurant. Dress slightly smarter for a special mid-trip meal.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks brought to the secluded beach — sandwiches, fruit, and cold water from a local mini-market (~€6-10)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a top-rated local seafood taverna. Whole grilled fish, prawns saganaki, and a bottle of local white wine (~€35-45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a great day to treat yourself slightly more at dinner as a mid-trip celebration. Make a reservation in advance for the seafood restaurant.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or stretching on the beach at sunrise if the resort or a local instructor offers it. Otherwise, take an early morning walk along the coastline before the heat builds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive oil producer or honey farm if one is accessible nearby. Learn about traditional production methods and taste the products.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the harbour in the evening and watch the fishing boats. Stop at a waterfront café for a cold drink and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast — Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts at a café (~€6-8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a casual taverna near the farm or countryside. Try horiatiki (village salad) and grilled bread with olive oil (~€12-16 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant with live traditional Greek music if available. Try beef stifado (slow-cooked stew) or chicken lemon rice soup (~€20-26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check with the resort concierge about local farm visits or food producers — many offer informal tastings for a small fee or free.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer boat excursion to a nearby island or uninhabited islet for the day. Enjoy pristine beaches and snorkeling in untouched waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the island or islet. Find a shaded spot for a midday rest, then swim again in the afternoon when the light turns golden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by ferry or boat. Shower and enjoy a quiet evening at the resort bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch or eat at a small beach taverna on the island if available (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby pizzeria/pasta place for a change of pace (~€16-22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the island boat trip in advance. Bring extra water, snacks, sunscreen, and a towel. Check the return boat schedule carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local town on foot. Visit a small local museum, a historic church, or a traditional craft workshop to connect with the local culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort beach. Try a water sport you haven't tried yet — windsurfing, jet skiing, or parasailing (~€20-40).
day_by_day.evening: Browse local shops for handmade ceramics, jewellery, or food products as gifts or souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in town — try bougatsa (custard or cheese pastry) with coffee (~€5-8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a popular local spot recommended by a local. Try fresh grilled fish or a seafood pasta (~€16-20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop or terrace restaurant with sea views. Order mixed grill platter and local beer or wine (~€22-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ask locals or hotel staff for their personal restaurant recommendations — these often lead to the best hidden gems.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim before breakfast — the sea is calmest and most beautiful at dawn. Enjoy the beach nearly to yourself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely drive or taxi to a different part of the coastline you haven't visited yet. Explore a new beach or fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final proper splurge dinner at one of the area's best-regarded restaurants — a fitting reward for a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast to start the day well (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harbourside café in the new fishing village. Try freshly made fish soup or grilled sardines with lemon (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual dinner at a highly recommended local restaurant. Try lamb slow-roasted with herbs, accompanied by local wine (~€30-40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to revisit any favourite spots or beaches from earlier in the trip. Start thinking about any last-minute souvenirs to pick up.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim and beach session. Soak up every last moment of the warm Aegean Sea and sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack non-essential items and do a final walk through the local village. Pick up any remaining souvenirs — local olive oil, herbs, honey, or ceramics make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favourite restaurant from the trip, or try somewhere new recommended by a local you've met during your stay.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed resort breakfast (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café — Greek salad, fresh bread, and cold lemonade (~€12-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — return to your favourite taverna or try a new spot. Share several mezze dishes and toast with ouzo or local wine (~€25-35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time for the next day. Arrange airport transfer in advance if not already done. Keep one set of fresh clothes accessible for the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final slow breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk along the beach or sit on the terrace with a coffee, absorbing the view before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Transfer to the airport with time to spare. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Greek products — olive oil, wine, or local sweets like loukoumades or mastiha.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories, a sun-kissed glow, and a taste for Greek food that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort — make it a good one (~€10-14 if not included)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a quick souvlaki stop on the way (~€8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Double-check all luggage weight limits, especially if you've bought local food products. Keep all travel documents easily accessible.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront suite, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation stroll along the resort's private beach. Take a leisurely swim in the warm Aegean Sea, unwind on a sun lounger with complimentary chilled towels and refreshments provided by the resort's beach butler service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's cliffside or beachfront bar. Enjoy the golden hour over the sea before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant – fresh grilled sea bream, Greek salad with barrel-aged feta, and chilled white Assyrtiko wine from Santorini
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant – tasting menu featuring local mezedes, slow-roasted lamb with herbs, and loukoumades with thyme honey for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Confirm beach butler service upon arrival. Keep the first evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a private guided snorkeling tour along a nearby secluded cove. Explore crystal-clear waters teeming with Mediterranean marine life with professional equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht or catamaran half-day charter departing from the nearest marina. Sail to hidden sea caves and a remote turquoise bay for swimming and sunbathing. A crew member serves chilled champagne and light bites on board.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa treatment – opt for a traditional Greek olive oil and honey body wrap or a deep-tissue massage at the resort's luxury spa.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the resort terrace – fresh yogurt with Cretan thyme honey, loukoumades, smoked salmon, local cheeses, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light mezedes and fresh fruit served on the yacht – tzatziki, dolmades, grilled octopus skewers, and local olives
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium nearby taverna renowned for fresh catch – whole grilled lobster, kritharoto (orzo risotto with seafood), and a bottle of Domaine Sigalas Santorini white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter in advance through the resort's concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling and sailing.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic village with a dedicated expert historian guide. Explore ruins, temples, or traditional whitewashed architecture at a relaxed pace with no crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan market or ceramics workshop in a nearby village. Watch craftspeople at work and select handmade souvenirs. Followed by a visit to a local olive oil estate for a premium tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the resort's private terrace with panoramic sea views. Enjoy curated Greek spirits – mastiha liqueur, ouzo, or a local craft gin with artisan nibbles.

meals.breakfast: In-suite private breakfast – continental spread with fresh pastries, local honey, fruit platters, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a family-run taverna in the village – moussaka, spanakopita, grilled halloumi, and village bread with local olive oil
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner arranged by the resort – a bespoke candlelit table on the sand with a personalized 5-course menu and sommelier-selected Greek wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the archaeological site. The private beach dinner must be pre-arranged with the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or Pilates session on the beach or resort pavilion led by a private instructor. Follow with a refreshing swim in the Aegean and a peaceful walk along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive private cooking class with a local Greek chef. Learn to prepare traditional dishes from scratch – fresh pasta, spanakopita, grilled fish with ladolemono, and a classic Greek dessert like galaktoboureko.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class at a private dinner setting arranged by the chef, paired with selected Greek wines.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast – acai bowl, avocado toast on sourdough, smoked mackerel, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – grilled vegetable platter, hummus with warm pita, and a fresh watermelon and feta salad
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the cooking class, served in a private dining room or terrace with curated Greek wine pairings selected by the instructor

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class through the resort concierge or a local culinary school. Classes typically last 3–4 hours including the meal.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private boat excursion begins with morning departure. Cruise to a stunning secluded beach or island nearby, accessible only by sea. Swim, snorkel, and relax in complete privacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat journey to a second scenic stop – a sea cave or a charming fishing village with a small harbor. Explore on foot and browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a private sunset cocktail experience on the boat before docking, or watch the sunset from the resort's elevated terrace.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure – eggs benedict, fresh fruit, pastries, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef and enjoyed on the boat or beach – charcuterie, artisan cheeses, marinated seafood, fresh bread, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's seafood-focused restaurant – fresh catch of the day, grilled calamari, sea urchin pasta, and a dessert of fresh figs with mastiha ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen generously throughout the day on the water. Bring a light cover-up, sunhat, and polarized sunglasses. Inform the concierge of any dietary preferences for the picnic basket.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort's infinity pool or private beach. Enjoy a luxury spa facial or hydrotherapy session at the resort spa to recharge midway through the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine tasting experience at a nearby premium winery. Tour the vineyard, learn about indigenous Greek grape varieties such as Assyrtiko, Xinomavro, and Agiorgitiko, and taste 5–6 curated wines with local cheese and charcuterie pairings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a cocktail at the bar and take in the night sky from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort terrace breakfast – Greek yogurt parfait, smoked salmon bagel, seasonal fruit, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Wine tasting paired lunch at the winery – mezedes, aged local cheeses, cured meats, marinated olives, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at a highly rated local restaurant – lamb chops with rosemary and lemon, roasted vegetables, tzatziki, and a bottle of Naoussa Xinomavro red wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transport to and from the winery. Request a sommelier-led tasting for the most immersive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking or paddleboarding along the coastline with a private guide. Explore sea arches, hidden inlets, and dramatic rock formations in the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Greek monastery or hilltop chapel nearby for a cultural and spiritual experience. Enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding landscape and sea.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury resort spa evening – couple's massage or solo deep relaxation treatment, followed by a soak in a private hot tub or outdoor jacuzzi overlooking the sea.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before kayaking – granola, Greek yogurt, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming cliffside or hilltop restaurant near the monastery – slow-cooked goat stifado, village salad, and fresh bread with olive oil
meals.dinner: In-room private dining experience – the resort chef prepares a personalized 4-course menu served on your suite's private terrace or balcony overlooking the sea

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking is best done early morning before the heat peaks. Dress modestly when visiting the monastery – shoulders and knees should be covered.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided food market tour in the nearest town or village. Explore stalls of fresh produce, local spices, honey, olives, and cheese with a knowledgeable local food guide who explains the history and use of each ingredient.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the resort's private beach with premium beach club service – chilled towels, cocktails, and a curated playlist. Optional: jet ski or water sports session in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private sunset sailing experience – a 2-hour golden hour cruise along the coastline with champagne and canapés served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – shakshuka with local tomatoes and herbs, fresh pastries, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Tasting spread assembled from the morning market – fresh cheeses, cured meats, olives, seasonal fruit, and artisan bread enjoyed in a scenic spot
meals.dinner: Dinner at a celebrated seafront restaurant – grilled whole fish, seafood risotto, and a dessert of baklava with pistachio and rosewater ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Bring a reusable bag to the market for any purchases. The sunset sailing cruise should be booked in advance through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by private vehicle to a renowned nearby beach rated among Greece's most beautiful – think turquoise lagoons, white pebbles, or pink sand depending on the region. Arrive early before day visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the beach area – swim, snorkel, or simply relax under a private umbrella with a butler service if available. Explore a nearby coastal village on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in time for sunset. Enjoy a nightcap at the resort bar and reflect on the day's scenery.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – eggs any style, Greek pastries, fresh juice, and strong coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside taverna near the day-trip destination – fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and chilled local beer or white wine
meals.dinner: Resort dinner at the chef's table experience – an intimate 6-course tasting menu with the head chef explaining each dish and its local provenance

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (by 8:30 AM) to beat the crowds at popular beaches. Pack a beach bag with sunscreen, water, and a good book. The chef's table experience requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hiking or nature walk through a scenic coastal trail or olive grove landscape. A local naturalist guide explains the flora, fauna, and history of the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Indulge in a luxury spa ritual – a 90-minute Greek ritual combining a sea salt scrub, olive oil massage, and cooling aloe wrap.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional Greek music and dance performance arranged by the resort – an authentic cultural evening with live bouzouki, folk dancing, and local performers.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast – poached eggs, avocado, smoked trout, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at the resort pool bar – club sandwich with local ingredients, fresh lemonade, and a Greek mezedes platter
meals.dinner: Dinner at an acclaimed local restaurant with a focus on Cretan or regional cuisine – dakos, slow-baked lamb with artichokes, and local wine from the region

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy footwear and bring water and a sun hat for the morning hike. The cultural performance is typically arranged for 2–3 hours in the evening and is a highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Chartered seaplane or helicopter scenic flight over the Greek coastline and nearby islands (subject to availability in the region). A breathtaking aerial perspective of the turquoise Aegean, volcanic caldera, or island clusters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and spend the afternoon at leisure – lounge by the pool, enjoy a book, or browse the resort's boutique. Optional: private photography session on the beach with a professional photographer to capture memories.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style luxury dinner at the resort's most exclusive restaurant or a nearby Michelin-recommended establishment – a celebration of Greek gastronomy.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the suite terrace – croissants, smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, fresh fruit, and a glass of Prosecco or local sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – sushi-grade tuna tartare, cold gazpacho, and a fresh green salad with lemon vinaigrette
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course dinner at a top-rated restaurant – langoustine carpaccio, truffle-infused lamb, aged Greek cheese board, and a dessert of chocolate fondant with mastiha cream, paired with a premium Greek wine flight

day_by_day.notes: The scenic flight must be booked well in advance and is weather-dependent. Confirm availability with the concierge at the start of the trip. The professional photography session typically lasts 1–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim and snorkel in the Aegean from the resort's private beach. Collect sea glass or shells as natural souvenirs. Enjoy a slow, mindful start to the last full day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan studio or gallery – purchase handcrafted jewelry, ceramics, or artwork as premium keepsakes. Followed by a stroll through a charming nearby village with a gelato or local sweet treat stop.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's rooftop or elevated terrace. Toast to the trip with a curated Greek cocktail – a mastiha sour, ouzo spritz, or a bespoke creation by the resort's mixologist.

meals.breakfast: Full leisurely resort breakfast – the complete spread including eggs, pastries, cheese, cold cuts, fresh juices, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beloved local spot – slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, horiatiki salad, and warm pita with taramasalata and melitzanosalata
meals.dinner: Final dinner at the resort's signature restaurant – a curated Greek tasting menu celebrating the best of the trip's culinary journey, with a personalized dessert and a farewell note from the chef

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to complete any last-minute shopping for gifts and souvenirs. Confirm departure logistics with the resort concierge – arrange the private transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach or a quiet moment on the suite's private terrace. Pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy a last Greek coffee and a sweet pastry from the resort café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to the airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, flavors, culture, and Aegean beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry the warmth of Greece home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a light but indulgent spread of yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, warm pastries, and a farewell glass of fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Depending on flight time – either a light lunch at an airport lounge or a packed gourmet snack box prepared by the resort chef for the journey
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort if your flight allows – many luxury resorts accommodate this for premium guests. Tip the resort staff who made your stay exceptional. Keep all receipts for VAT refund eligibility on purchases made in Greece.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC
